name: Partial Bilateral Aplasia of the Müllerian Ducts

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Müllerian Duct Anomalies

criteria.description: Radiological evidence of partial bilateral absence or hypoplasia of the Müllerian ducts on MRI or ultrasound
Presence of primary amenorrhea in adolescent females with normal secondary sexual characteristics
Normal development of external genitalia with absent or hypoplastic uterus and upper two-thirds of the vagina
Exclusion of associated renal tract anomalies by imaging

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of primary amenorrhea with radiological confirmation of partial bilateral aplasia of the Müllerian ducts and normal external genitalia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other causes of primary amenorrhea and Müllerian anomalies.

pathognomonic.notes: Absence of menarche by age 15 or within 3 years of thelarche

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypoplasia or aplasia of the uterus
Hypoplasia or aplasia of the upper two-thirds of the vagina
pathognomonic.notes: Partial vaginal agenesis or shortened vaginal canal

common.notes: Normal breast development and pubic hair
Due to obstructed menstrual flow in some cases
Due to uterine hypoplasia or aplasia

occasional.notes: May include unilateral renal agenesis or ectopia

searchTerms: psychological issues related to inability to conceive

occasional.notes: Painful intercourse due to vaginal hypoplasia

rare.notes: Due to retrograde menstruation in obstructive cases

laboratory: Normal female hormone profile (FSH, LH, estradiol)
imaging: MRI pelvis showing partial bilateral aplasia or hypoplasia of the uterus and upper vagina
Ultrasound demonstrating absent or rudimentary uterine structures
Renal ultrasound to exclude associated anomalies
genetic: No specific gene identified; sporadic or multifactorial etiology suspected
other: Normal external genitalia on physical examination

distinguishingFeatures: Complete absence of uterus and upper vagina
Similar presentation but more extensive anatomical absence
Female external genitalia with absent uterus
Presence of uterus and normal endometrium
Obstructive vaginal septum visible on imaging
Cyclic pelvic pain with normal menstruation

redFlags: Primary amenorrhea with absent uterus on imaging
Normal secondary sexual characteristics with absent menstrual bleeding
Presence of renal anomalies associated with reproductive tract malformations
references: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 94: Mullerian Agenesis: Diagnosis and Management
Orphanet Report on Müllerian Duct Anomalies, ORPHA:180068
Rock JA, et al. Mullerian Anomalies: Diagnosis and Management. Obstet Gynecol Clin North Am. 2017
